# Chapter 4: System Design

## Overview

This chapter presents the system design for the proposed cardiopulmonary sound separation prototype. The design translates the requirements from Chapter 3 into system-level diagrams, use case descriptions, module responsibilities, sequence flow, and interface planning. The design remains implementation-ready but does not claim that the final prototype has already been built or tested.

The proposed system accepts a mixed cardiopulmonary audio file, validates and preprocesses the recording, runs a machine learning-based separation workflow, and returns separated heart and lung sound outputs to the user.

## Context Diagram

Figure @fig-context-diagram shows the system context. The main external actor is the user, who uploads the mixed audio file and receives separated outputs. The system may also use public datasets during development and evaluation, but the user-facing workflow remains focused on uploaded audio processing.

![Context diagram for the proposed cardiopulmonary sound separation prototype](figures/plantuml/context_diagram.png){#fig-context-diagram}

## Use Case Diagram

Figure @fig-use-case-diagram shows the main user interactions supported by the proposed prototype. The use cases cover upload, validation, preprocessing, sound separation, result viewing, output download, and optional processing history.

![Use case diagram for the proposed cardiopulmonary sound separation prototype](figures/plantuml/use_case_diagram.png){#fig-use-case-diagram}

### Use Case Description

Table @tbl-use-case-description describes the main use case for separating a mixed cardiopulmonary recording.

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Use case name | Separate cardiopulmonary sound recording |
| Primary actor | Student or researcher user |
| Goal | Obtain separated heart and lung sound outputs from one mixed cardiopulmonary recording |
| Trigger | The user uploads a supported audio file and starts processing |
| Main output | Heart sound output file, lung sound output file, and processing status |

: Main use case description for the proposed prototype {#tbl-use-case-description}

#### Actors

The primary actor is the student or researcher user. The user interacts with the prototype through the interface by uploading an audio file, starting processing, viewing results, and downloading outputs.

The system components include the user interface, audio validation module, preprocessing module, separation model module, result management module, and storage component. These are internal system elements and are not treated as separate external users.

#### Preconditions

The user must have a cardiopulmonary audio file in a supported format. The prototype must be available, and the separation model or processing pipeline must be configured. If a processing history feature is included, temporary or persistent storage must also be available.

#### Normal Flow

1. The user opens the prototype interface.
2. The user uploads a mixed cardiopulmonary audio file.
3. The system validates the file format, file size, and readability.
4. The system preprocesses the audio to prepare it for separation.
5. The system runs the separation workflow.
6. The system generates heart and lung sound outputs.
7. The system displays the processing result.
8. The user downloads the separated outputs.

#### Postconditions

After successful processing, the user receives separated heart and lung sound output files. The system may store basic processing history if the feature is implemented and if storage and privacy constraints are satisfied.

#### Alternative Flows and Exceptions

If the uploaded file is unsupported or unreadable, the system rejects the file and displays a clear error message. If preprocessing fails, the system stops the separation workflow and informs the user. If the separation model fails to produce valid outputs, the system reports the failure and avoids presenting incomplete files as successful results. If storage is unavailable, the system may still allow output download for the current session without saving history.

#### Non-Functional Requirements

The use case must support usability, reliability, maintainability, performance, privacy, and compatibility requirements. The interface should be easy to follow, errors should be understandable, and uploaded files should be handled carefully. The design should also keep audio handling, preprocessing, model execution, and result management modular so that the prototype can be maintained and extended during FYP2.

## Activity Diagram

Figure @fig-activity-diagram shows the activity flow for the main sound separation workflow. The flow starts with audio upload and validation, then continues to preprocessing, separation, output generation, and download.

![Activity diagram for the sound separation workflow](figures/plantuml/activity_diagram.png){#fig-activity-diagram}

## Class Diagram

Figure @fig-class-diagram shows the planned class-level structure for the prototype. The classes represent the main responsibilities of the system rather than final implementation code. The design separates upload handling, validation, preprocessing, model execution, result management, and processing records.

![Class diagram for the planned prototype modules](figures/plantuml/class_diagram.png){#fig-class-diagram}

Table @tbl-system-modules summarizes the main system modules and responsibilities.

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| User interface | Provides upload controls, processing status, result display, and output download. |
| Audio validation module | Checks file type, size, readability, and basic audio metadata. |
| Preprocessing module | Prepares the audio for separation through required cleaning or transformation steps. |
| Separation model module | Runs the selected machine learning-based separation workflow. |
| Result management module | Stores output paths, exposes downloads, and reports processing status. |
| Storage component | Handles uploaded files, temporary files, output files, and optional processing history. |

: Main system modules and responsibilities {#tbl-system-modules}

## Sequence Diagram

Figure @fig-sequence-diagram shows the planned interaction sequence between the user interface and the major system modules. The sequence highlights that validation must succeed before preprocessing and separation are attempted.

![Sequence diagram for uploading and separating a cardiopulmonary recording](figures/plantuml/sequence_diagram.png){#fig-sequence-diagram}

## Interface Design

The interface design should support the core workflow without unnecessary complexity. The first screen should allow the user to select an audio file and start processing. The processing view should show validation and processing status. The result view should provide separate heart and lung output sections with download controls.

Table @tbl-interface-areas summarizes the planned interface areas.

| Interface area | Planned content |
|---|---|
| Upload area | File selector, accepted format note, and start processing control. |
| Status area | Validation status, preprocessing status, separation status, and error messages. |
| Result area | Heart sound output, lung sound output, and download controls. |
| History area | Optional list of previous processing records if the feature is included. |

: Planned interface areas for the prototype {#tbl-interface-areas}

No final interface screenshots are presented in this FYP1 report because the implementation stage has not been completed yet. The interface design will be refined during FYP2 implementation.

## Summary

This chapter presented the system design for the proposed prototype, including the context diagram, use case diagram, use case description, activity diagram, class diagram, sequence diagram, module responsibilities, and planned interface areas. The next chapter defines the implementation plan for developing, testing, deploying, documenting, and maintaining the prototype.
